Solver tournaments beat quantum hype is not a slogan; it is a delivery position. We keep seeing the same economics: teams that internalize this spend their budget on value, while teams that ignore it spend on rework and explanations.

items: Optimization is where quantum methods earn money today; formulation honesty decides where.
Negative results are deliverables: an improved classical baseline is a win you keep.
Revisit triggers tied to hardware roadmaps keep closed cases honest.

blocks.x: Three questions to ask your current vendors

items: What is the classical baseline every proposed capability must beat, measured on identical data?
Which named individual owns the control environment around this capability — not the function, the person?
Show us a negative result you documented — the discipline is the product.

blocks.x: The expensive mistake is measurement retrofits: without the baseline locked in week one, every outcome claim becomes an argument instead of an audit, and the program loses its budget defense.

items: falsifiable criteria and locked baselines before build; the demo is the least important artifact.
named owners, run models and escalation paths agreed with the operating team, not for it.
replay trails, control tests and documentation as artifacts of the build — never reconstructed.

blocks.x: Industrialized winners typically compress solve time from minutes to seconds on planning problems.
